differences.title: 1. CORE ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: Wails embeds a Go application and uses the OS's native WebView, minimizing binary size and startup time by leveraging existing system components.
differences.rightDesc: Electron bundles Node.js and a full Chromium browser instance, offering extensive APIs but resulting in larger applications and higher memory usage.

differences.title: 2. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Wails benefits from Go's fast compilation and startup, and native WebView's efficiency, leading to quicker application launches and reduced resource footprint.
differences.rightDesc: Electron's bundled Chromium and Node.js require significant initialization time and resources, leading to slower startup compared to native solutions.

differences.title: 3. BINARY SIZE
differences.leftDesc: Wails compiles Go code directly and relies on the OS's WebView, producing significantly smaller executable files suitable for distribution.
differences.rightDesc: Electron applications include Node.js runtime and Chromium, leading to substantial executable sizes, often hundreds of megabytes.

differences.title: 4. MEMORY USAGE
differences.leftDesc: By using native WebViews and a Go backend, Wails consumes less memory as it doesn't bundle a complete browser engine.
differences.rightDesc: Electron's embedded Chromium process is a significant consumer of RAM, often leading to higher memory footprints for applications.

differences.title: 5. DEVELOPMENT EXPERIENCE
differences.leftDesc: Combines Go for backend logic with standard web technologies (HTML, CSS, JS/TS) for UI, offering strong typing and efficient concurrency.
differences.rightDesc: Leverages familiar web development stack (HTML, CSS, JS/TS) with Node.js, providing a vast ecosystem but potentially less structured backend.

differences.title: 6. NATIVE INTEGRATION
differences.leftDesc: Wails allows direct, high-performance interaction between Go and JavaScript via efficient binding generation, enabling seamless native feature access.
differences.rightDesc: Electron provides a rich set of Node.js APIs to interact with the OS, but direct native module integration can be more complex.

differences.title: 7. ECOSYSTEM & COMMUNITY
differences.leftDesc: Wails leverages the robust Go ecosystem for backend and the vast web frontend community, with a rapidly developing framework.
differences.rightDesc: Electron benefits from the massive JavaScript/Node.js ecosystem and a large, established community, offering extensive third-party libraries.
